title: ADVISOR: Approximate Computing-frienDly High-LeVel Synthesis DesIgn Space ExplORer
problem: High-level synthesis (HLS) enables rapid exploration of hardware implementations, but when combined with approximate computing trade-offs, each design variant must be fully approximated to evaluate area/power vs. accuracy trade-offs, resulting in prohibitively long exploration time.
motivation: Approximate computing allows area/power savings but requires identifying which hardware implementations have the highest potential for approximation; HLS design space exploration is slow when every design must be fully approximated.
method: ADVISOR uses a fast scoring system called the Approximation Friendliness Index (AFI) to predict which hardware designs will work well with approximation (reducing precision to trade accuracy for speed and power). Instead of fully approximating every design variant—which is computationally expensive—it only applies the full approximation process to designs with high AFI scores. This filtering approach lets the tool explore 68 times faster than exhaustive exploration, because it avoids wasting computation on designs unlikely to benefit from approximation.
key_novelty: A static scoring metric (AFI) that quickly identifies which hardware designs will benefit most from approximation, eliminating the need to fully approximate every design variant during exploration.
contributions: AFI metric for statically evaluating approximation potential in HLS-generated designs
Automated HLS design space explorer that achieves 68x speedup over exhaustive approximation
Demonstration of equivalent results to exhaustive search with dramatically reduced runtime

metrics.other: equivalent accuracy results to full exploration
